transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-05 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Alex Johnson (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Aurora ML Eng), Marcus Velez (Aurora Infra), Sofia Chen (Aurora CTO)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): Deep dive on kernel selection and profiling; decided on follow-ups to run TensorRT-LLM and vLLM side-by-side with CUDA Graphs enabled, share traces and security docs.

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you carving out time, quick round of intros?
00:07 Lena (Aurora): hi lena here, i'm the ml engineer owning the inference pipelines for recommendations, we hit latency spikes when we bump to longer contexts, so keen to understand kernel selection and caching.
00:18 Marcus (Aurora): marcus infra, i'll be responsible for the VPC/on-prem footprint and networking, also curious about GPU memory patterns.
00:25 Sofia (Aurora): sofia, cto, i'll listen for operational risks and quantization impact on accuracy.
00:32 Alex: great, priya will run the deep dive on runtime profiling and kernels, i'll handle next steps and commercial bits. priya over to you.
00:40 Priya (Redwood SE): cool thanks, so agenda: 1) show profiler traces we ran on 70B-ish LLM, 2) kernel selection behavior (cuBLAS vs custom kernels), 3) TensorRT-LLM (we'll call it "TRT-LLM") vs vLLM comparisons, 4) CUDA Graphs effect on small vs large batches, 5) KV cache warm/cold behavior, 6) quantization impacts. any additions?
01:02 Lena: sounds good, please call out when stuff is speculative vs measured.
01:07 Priya: absolutely. starting with profiling - here are two traces: one from a hosted run on A100 with TRT-LLM optimized kernels, one from a v l l m run (note: transcript for vLLM sometimes shows as v l m in our docs) on same hardware. we saw that kernel selection moves between cuBLAS GEMM kernels for matmul and a fused attention kernel on TRT optimized path.
01:30 Priya: (slight noise) you can see at the 300-800ms region the attention kernel dominates when sequence len > 1024. on vllm traces the KV cache lookups were more frequent - looks like vllm didn't fuse as many attention kernels, so higher kernel launch overhead.
01:52 Marcus: can you quantify overhead? like percent latency from kernel-launch vs compute?
01:56 Priya: yes, in our traces kernel-launch/dispatch accounted for ~12-18% of end-to-end token latency on vllm for medium batches (batch 4-8), vs ~5-7% on TRT-LLM due to fused kernels and fewer launches plus cudagraphs. caveat: these are with TensorRT kernels tuned for that model variant.
02:22 Lena: and memory usage? we saw our OOMs when enabling 8k context for 70B.
02:28 Priya: with TRT-LLM + quant 4-bit we reduced peak by ~35% in this profile; vllm with 8-bit quant saw ~22% reduction but had higher activation memory because of per-layer buffers. also note CPU-side staging of KV cache in v l l m sometimes showed swapping spikes on our infra tests.
02:49 Alex: quick Q for sofia on accuracy tradeoffs you flagged - is 4-bit acceptable? what are your guardrails?
02:55 Sofia: we have an internal eval set; anything that causes >1.5% drop in top-1 for our intent classifier is a blocker. we want to see token-level log-prob drift metrics.
03:06 Priya: noted. we'll attach eval diffs to the benchmark spreadsheet.
03:12 Priya: next, CUDA Graphs - when we pre-capture the execution graph for fixed-length batched workloads, we saw latency p50 drop by 18-25% on TRT-LLM and 10-15% on vllm. the difference stems from TRT kernels already being fused so cudagraphs has less to optimize on, but the reduced launch overhead matters more for vllm.
03:36 Marcus: any caveats for dynamic shapes? our requests vary between 256 and 4096 tokens.
03:42 Priya: cudagraphs works best when you can bucket by shape or use a small number of capture variants. for highly dynamic shapes you either accept more capture variants or fall back to non-captured path which loses the gain. we recommend shape bucketing and a warm-up policy for prod.
03:58 Lena: ok, talk to me about KV cache warm vs cold - we see initial tokens are slow, then faster. can caching be persisted across requests?
04:06 Priya: two points: 1) KV cache warm-ups - first generation populates cache and causes higher latency; prefix caching and reuse between related requests helps. 2) persistence - in dedicated/on-prem you can pin a session or reuse KV cache in memory between requests on the same GPU, but that requires sticky routing (we can do session affinity at the routing layer). sticky routing has throughput tradeoffs vs cache re-use.
04:35 Marcus: sticky routing means less bin-packing across GPUs?
04:39 Priya: exactly, you trade off 10-30% throughput efficiency for lower token latency depending on workload. for some low-latency features it's worth it.
04:47 Lena: how about disk-backed KV for very large contexts? we have guests that want 32k.
04:51 Priya: we don't recommend disk-backed KV for hot path; you'll kill latency. better approaches: model quantization + sharded KV across GPUs or async prefix fetch that overlaps I/O with compute.
05:05 Alex: let's pivot to kernel selection detail - what drives selecting cuBLAS vs TRT custom kernels?
05:12 Priya: two main heuristics: operator shape (matmul sizes), sequence length distribution, and whether kernels have fused attention implementations for that model topology. TRT-LLM often provides fused attention and grouped GEMMs so the runtime picks them for large heads/sequence lengths. vllm tends to use general-purpose kernels and relies on efficient batching and KV reuse.
05:36 Marcus: any pointers to our infra team about enabling these kernels on our on-prem GPUs? we run a mix of H100 and A100.
05:43 Priya: yes, TRT-LLM requires TensorRT compatible drivers and matching cuDNN/TensorRT versions. for H100 there are newer builds; for A100 you'll want the TRT version we tested (we'll include exact versions in the doc). vLLM is more portable but may not have the same fused kernels. if you need the TRT kernel set on-prem we can help with a compatibility matrix.
06:05 Lena: model variants - you mentioned model-specific kernels. if we change model versions often, is that an operational headache?
06:12 Priya: slightly. TRT kernels are often built per-model or per-architecture/sequence tradeoff. we recommend a CI step that runs a quick profiling to validate kernel selection after a model update. Redwood Optimize can automate that.
06:28 Alex: question from chat - what about quantization: 4-bit vs 8-bit?
06:32 Priya: 4-bit quant (GPTQ or similar) gives best memory savings and cost reduction but can introduce accuracy drift; 8-bit is safer in many cases. TRT-LLM supports int8 pathways and we have mixed-precision fused kernels for 4-bit in experimental builds. we'll provide accuracy vs perf curves per model.
06:55 Sofia: please include the evaluation harness and seed so we can reproduce.
06:58 Priya: yes we'll attach the eval harness and exact random seeds.
07:02 Priya: live demo of traces - i'm going to share the profiling screenshot, you'll see timeline rows per GPU op. (screen share noise) there are spikes at 1.2s where a fallback path executed for long sequences - that's the non-fused attention path.
07:23 Lena: is fallback a runtime decision? can we force the fused kernel?
07:27 Priya: it's runtime-based; it chooses the most compatible kernel. you can force kernel path at deployment but that risks correctness if the kernel isn't compatible for some shapes. safer is to pre-quant and run a quick canary.
07:42 Marcus: we saw transient CUDA launch failures in earlier tests, any mitigation?
07:46 Priya: those were driver mismatches and a race in memory allocation; we fixed by pinning driver versions and using a memory defragmentation hook in startup; we'll supply recommended driver + runtime versions.
07:59 Alex: let's talk throughput - how to pick batch sizes?
08:03 Priya: for p99-sensitive features, smaller batch sizes reduce tail latency but increase cost; for throughput-driven offline workloads, larger batches with cudagraphs give best cost/token. our rule of thumb: aim for batch sizes that fill the compute but keep p50 under your SLO. we'll give a chart mapping batch size to p50/p95/p99 from our tests.
08:26 Lena: any specific numbers from your 70B test?
08:30 Priya: p50 at batch 1 was 180ms, batch 8 p50 95ms, but p99 for batch 8 increased to 420ms due to queueing. with cudagraphs enabled p50 for batch 8 dropped to 78ms and p99 to 330ms.
08:49 Marcus: does cudagraphs interact poorly with multi-tenant GPU sharing? we co-locate multiple models per node.
08:56 Priya: it's ok as long as capture variants are limited; the capture adds memory overhead and traces are per process. co-locating many models increases memory pressure and capture count; we'd recommend dedicated pools or bin-packing policies that isolate high-sensitivity endpoints.
09:15 Alex: quick break then we'll go into a plan for running a side-by-side pilot.
09:22 (brief pause)
09:44 Priya: pilot plan: 1) Redwood runs TRT-LLM build + cudagraphs on your sample workload in our staging (hosted) and provides traces; 2) Redwood runs vLLM optimized run on same workload; 3) Aurora runs on-prem pilot with sticky routing and one capture variant for common shape; 4) compare accuracy, p50/p99, and cost.
10:16 Marcus: timeline?
10:18 Alex: we propose initial hosted runs by 2026-08-07, on-prem pilot start 2026-08-18 (two-week run), results review 2026-09-02.
10:28 Lena: sounds good, need to lock down dataset and eval harness.
10:32 Alex: action item for Marcus to provide dataset access.
10:36 Marcus: will do.
10:39 Priya: one more topic - observability traces: Redwood console can surface token-level latency, per-kernel flame graphs, and KV cache hit/miss rates. we can also export raw nvprof-like traces.
10:55 Lena: can we get RBAC and audit logs for the on-prem control plane?
10:58 Alex: yes - that's part of our Private offering; we'll share the SOC2 docs and an example RBAC policy.
11:05 Sofia: on security we also need KMS integration for model keys and an HSM option.
11:09 Alex: noted, we'll include KMS/HSM options and the integration guide.
11:14 Priya: quick note on compatibility: for H100 TRT-LLM requires CUDA/driver versions X.Y.Z (we'll attach exact), and for A100 the tested combination was A.B.C. wrong combos lead to kernel crashes.
11:29 Marcus: please include a short checklist for on-prem runbook - driver, cudnn, tensorRT, kernel build steps.
11:35 Priya: will do.
11:38 Alex: any final questions?
11:41 Lena: one: is there a simple heuristic to decide TRT vs vLLM for a new feature?
11:45 Priya: if you need best in class latency with high concurrency and can run the TRT stack on your infra, TRT-LLM + cudagraphs + quantization tends to win. if you prefer portability and faster model churn, vllm is easier to deploy. if uncertain, run the side-by-side pilot.
11:59 Alex: recap and next steps: 1) Redwood to send benchmark spreadsheet + profiling traces (Alex) 2) Priya to run CUDA Graphs capture and attach traces (Priya) 3) Marcus to provide dataset and infra access (Marcus) 4) schedule on-prem pilot start 2026-08-18.
12:22 Sofia: thanks all, appreciated.
12:26 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email.
